query: Describe the national (federal) government structure of Pakistan as of 2026-11-14. For each body in the executive, legislative and judicial branches, plus the national electoral authority, list its offices with: English and local-language title, how the OFFICE is filled (direct_election, indirect_election, appointment, mixed, hereditary, ex_officio), number of seats, term length, and the CURRENT holder(s) for single-seat or leadership offices only (head of state/government, presiding officer of each legislative chamber, president of the highest court, head of the electoral authority) with party and term start/end. For multi-member bodies give seat counts and selection method but do not list every member. Note recent reforms that changed how offices are filled (for example judicial elections). Also list the subnational tiers of government (first-level divisions, and municipal/local government) with counts. Give source URLs for every current officeholder.

offices.selection_details: Elected by the members of both Houses of Parliament and the four provincial assemblies; maximum two consecutive terms.

bodies.description: Head of state; normally acts on the advice of the Prime Minister/Cabinet.

offices.selection_details: Elected by the National Assembly from among its Muslim members and formally appointed by the President; tenure depends on Assembly confidence, with no fixed personal term.
Appointed by the President on the advice of the Prime Minister; 31 are listed in the Cabinet Division roster.
Appointed to ministerial office on the advice of the Prime Minister; 11 are listed in the published roster.

bodies.description: Prime Minister heads government; the Cabinet is collectively responsible to the National Assembly. Cabinet portfolio numbers are the published roster, not fixed constitutional strengths.

offices.title_en: Member of National Assembly, general seat
offices.selection_details: Single-member constituencies, direct plurality voting.

offices.title_en: Member of National Assembly, reserved seat for women
offices.title_local: رکن قومی اسمبلی، خواتین کی مخصوص نشست
offices.selection_details: Provincial party lists allocated proportionally to general seats won by political parties.

offices.title_en: Member of National Assembly, reserved seat for non-Muslims
offices.title_local: رکن قومی اسمبلی، غیر مسلموں کی مخصوص نشست
offices.selection_details: Party lists allocated proportionally on nationwide general-seat results.
Elected from the Assembly membership; continues until successor chosen subject to constitutional rules.

offices.title_en: Deputy Speaker of the National Assembly
offices.selection_details: Elected by the Assembly from its members.

bodies.description: Lower house; 336 membership seats. Speaker and deputy occupy seats already counted among members; the Assembly normally lasts five years unless dissolved.

offices.selection_details: 56 provincial and two capital general seats; elected by relevant assembly electoral colleges through proportional representation by single transferable vote.
Four from each province and one from the capital; elected by relevant electoral colleges.

offices.title_local: سینیٹر، ٹیکنوکریٹ یا علماء کی نشست
offices.selection_details: Four per province and one from the capital; indirect election.
One from each province; indirect election by provincial assembly.
Elected by senators from among themselves.
Elected by senators from among themselves.

bodies.description: Permanent upper house; 96 seats, with half the senators retiring every three years. Chairman and deputy chairman are already counted among the senators.

offices.title_en: Chief Justice of the Federal Constitutional Court
offices.title_local: وفاقی آئینی عدالت کے چیف جسٹس
offices.selection_details: President appoints under Article 175A; first chief exceptionally appointed on Prime Minister’s advice. Three years or retirement at 68, whichever earlier.

offices.title_en: Judge of the Federal Constitutional Court
offices.selection_details: Up to 12 other authorized positions (six filled as of the cutoff); nominated by the Judicial Commission and appointed by the President; serve until age 68 unless earlier departure.

bodies.description: Created by the Twenty-Seventh Amendment (2025); hears major constitutional matters formerly heard by the Supreme Court. Constitutional size is one chief justice plus judges set by Parliament or, pending legislation, the President. Thirteen authorized positions, seven reported filled on the cutoff. The inaugural chief and initial judges were exceptionally appointed by the President on prime-ministerial advice; later appointments follow the Judicial Commission procedure, not popular judicial elections.

offices.title_en: Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of Pakistan
offices.selection_details: President appoints following selection by a special parliamentary committee from the three most senior judges; term ends earlier on reaching 65.
Maximum 33 other judges by 2024 statute; Judicial Commission nominations and presidential appointment; retirement at age 65.

bodies.description: Highest ordinary appellate court, distinct from the constitutional court. Statute permits up to 33 judges in addition to the chief justice. The 2024 Twenty-Sixth Amendment changed chief-justice selection to a parliamentary committee choice from the three senior-most judges and capped the chief-justice term at three years; judges are appointed, not directly elected.

offices.title_en: Chief Justice of the Federal Shariat Court
offices.selection_details: Appointed by the President under Article 175A; term not exceeding three years, renewable.

offices.title_en: Judge of the Federal Shariat Court
offices.selection_details: Up to seven additional judges; appointed by the President under Article 175A for a term not exceeding three years, renewable.

bodies.description: Reviews whether specified laws conform to the injunctions of Islam; constitutional maximum eight judges, including its chief justice.

offices.title_en: Chief Justice of a High Court
offices.selection_details: Each court has a chief justice; appointed via constitutional Judicial Commission and President; normal retirement age 62.
Judicial Commission nomination and presidential appointment; regular retirement at age 62.

bodies.description: Five constitutional High Courts: one for each of the four provinces and one for Islamabad Capital Territory; their judges are appointed rather than popularly elected. Court-by-court judge strength is not uniformly established here.

offices.selection_details: President appoints after Prime Minister–opposition leader nominations, parliamentary committee hearing and confirmation; holds over until successor assumes office.
One from each province; nomination/confirmation process and appointment as provided in Articles 213 and 218; holdover until successor takes office.

bodies.description: Independent permanent national election-management authority of five members. After the 2024 amendment, a member whose five-year term expires continues until a successor enters office; the sitting chief commissioner was still listed after his original 2025 expiry.

structured_output.constitution_name: Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, 1973 (as amended through the Twenty-Seventh Amendment, 2025)

subnational_levels.description: Punjab, Sindh, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan; the Islamabad Capital Territory is separate, while Azad Jammu and Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan have distinct administrative arrangements.
Islamabad Capital Territory, Azad Jammu and Kashmir, and Gilgit-Baltistan; not three additional provinces.
Intermediate administrative units, not first-level federating units. Last nationwide official count verified is dated 1 March 2023; the 2026 total may differ.

Province-specific elected local-government structures include metropolitan or municipal corporations, municipal and town committees, and union, village or neighbourhood councils; no verified, consistent nationwide 2026 count of governing bodies. The 2023 census lists 650 urban areas, which must not be equated with 650 municipal governments.
